_comment: Single authored source record for the Kyverno board. scripts/gen_kyverno_board.py writes each skill's references/evidence-ledger.md from the rows that skill actually cites ([KYV-Exx] markers), so no skill ships an orphan source. Retrieved dates record when the maintainer read the source; release-pinned rows name the tag they were read at.

sources.claim: Kyverno v1.20.0 deletes the legacy kyverno.io policy engine, removes legacy execution from the admission, background and reports controllers, blocks creates and spec updates of legacy policy APIs, and makes the CLI reject legacy manifests in apply/test

Starting with v1.19 the admission controller and CLI emit deprecation warnings for legacy policies; the migration guide still prints the admission warning 'ClusterPolicy is deprecated and will be removed in a future release' and lists ClusterPolicy, Policy, PolicyException, CleanupPolicy and ClusterCleanupPolicy as legacy kinds; this wording lags the v1.20.0 removal in KYV-E01
At tag v1.20.0 the policies.kyverno.io CRDs serve v1, v1beta1 and v1alpha1; v1beta1 is the storage version and v1alpha1 is marked deprecated

ValidatingPolicy validationActions is a set drawn from Deny, Audit and Warn; failurePolicy is Ignore or Fail and defaults to Fail; failurePolicy governs evaluation errors, not validations that evaluate to false

ValidatingPolicy evaluation.admission.enabled and evaluation.background.enabled both default to true; background must be false when a rule uses variables only present in the admission request, such as the user name; evaluation.mode allows Kubernetes, HTTP or Envoy
webhookConfiguration.timeoutSeconds defaults to 10 seconds and must be between 1 and 30; after it expires the request may fail or ignore the policy result according to the failure policy
The Kyverno webhook controller registers separate '-ignore' and '-fail' validating webhook entries, so a policy's failurePolicy selects which webhook entry carries it
sources.section: webhook names built with -ignore and -fail suffixes (lines 200-209)

sources.claim: For admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 webhooks the default failurePolicy is Fail and timeoutSeconds defaults to 10 seconds within a 1 to 30 second range

Background scans do not block or delete existing resources even when a policy uses validationActions [Deny]; reports describe resources that exist in the cluster, and blocked requests are investigated through metrics and Kubernetes Events
Report results include pass, fail, warn (for example when policies.kyverno.io/scored is false) and error (an evaluation error prevented a normal result)
The minimum supported replica count for a highly available admission controller is three; leader election means one replica handles certificate and webhook management at a time

kyverno_admission_review_duration_seconds is the end-to-end admission review latency histogram and kyverno_admission_requests_total counts admission requests labelled by resource_kind, resource_request_operation and request_allowed

The v1 PolicyException spec requires policyRefs and offers matchConditions, images, allowedValues, validations (compensating controls), reportResult (skip or pass, default skip) and expiresAt (RFC3339; once expired it is no longer applied to incoming requests)

The CEL engine's exception lookup skips expired exceptions and matches exceptions to a policy only by policyRefs name and kind; the ValidatingPolicy, MutatingPolicy, ImageValidatingPolicy and DeletingPolicy reconcilers call it
The enablePolicyException flag defaults to false and exceptionNamespace defaults to empty; '*' allows exceptions in all namespaces

The policies.kyverno.io PolicyException works with all CEL policy types; compensating validations must all pass for the exception to be granted, otherwise the policy is evaluated as if the exception did not exist

ImageValidatingPolicy validationConfigurations mutateDigest, verifyDigest and required each default to true; cosign keyless identities match subject and issuer strictly, with subjectRegExp, issuerRegExp or a CEL subjectExpression as alternatives; in-toto attestations declare intoto.type

Image verification is invoked from CEL validations: verifyImageSignatures(image, attestors) and verifyAttestationSignatures(image, attestation, attestors) return counts, and extractPayload(image, attestation) exposes predicate content
ImageValidatingPolicy is Stable in v1.20.0 and does not pick up the admitted Pod's imagePullSecrets; private registry secrets must be listed in spec.credentials.secrets

GeneratingPolicy with a data source and synchronization deletes downstream resources on policy delete unless orphanDownstreamOnPolicyDelete is enabled; with a clone source, policy deletion retains downstream; trigger deletion with sync deletes downstream; generateExisting performs a one-time scan of existing triggers
sources.section: Synchronization with a Data Source / Clone Source; generateExisting

sources.claim: At v1.20.0 GeneratingPolicy evaluation.synchronize.enabled, evaluation.generateExisting.enabled and evaluation.orphanDownstreamOnPolicyDelete.enabled default to false, the orphan option applies only to data-type generation, and skipBackgroundRequests defaults to true

MutatingPolicy mutateExisting applies mutations to existing resources through background processing, usually needs extra RBAC for the background controller, and when trigger and target share a type mutates all matching existing resources on each trigger
DeletingPolicy is evaluated on a cron schedule with one-minute minimum granularity, performs destructive actions, and the cleanup controller needs get, list, watch and delete on the targets
In the kyverno CLI test file, operation UPDATE sets both object and oldObject to the same resource, and DELETE sets object to null; unset defaults to CREATE
kyverno test compares results declared ahead of time in a kyverno-test.yaml manifest with actual results, from a local folder or git repository

The generateValidatingAdmissionPolicy controller toggle defaults to true at v1.20.0, and an exception with compensating validations prevents translating its ValidatingPolicy into a native ValidatingAdmissionPolicy; the per-policy opt-in and the pod-controller autogen exclusion are in KYV-E37 and KYV-E40

Native ValidatingAdmissionPolicy is stable since Kubernetes v1.30, needs a ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding to take effect, and binding validationActions are Deny, Warn and Audit, where Deny and Warn cannot be combined

For legacy ClusterPolicy (v1.18 documentation) spec.failurePolicy defaults to Fail, webhookTimeoutSeconds defaults to 10 seconds within 1 to 30, and validationFailureAction is deprecated as of 1.13 in favour of per-rule failureAction
In ambient mode node-level ztunnel enforces L4 policy and the waypoint is the L7 proxy; a workload outside the mesh sends directly to the destination without traversing its waypoint

The istio.io/use-waypoint label records intent but does not guarantee traversal: ztunnel routes directly when the named waypoint is missing or the traffic type does not match, so its L7 policy never takes effect; binding status appears in the istio.io/WaypointBound condition
sources.section: Use a waypoint proxy; Require traffic to traverse the waypoint

sources.claim: istioctl analyze can run against a live cluster, local files (--use-kube=false, self-contained file set) or both
sources.section: Analyzing live clusters, local files, or both

sources.claim: An Istio canary upgrade runs the new revision beside the old one, moves namespaces by revision label or tag with workload restarts, and rolling back by uninstalling the canary does not revert gateways already upgraded in place
sources.section: Control plane; Data plane; Uninstall canary control plane

sources.claim: Istio's Gateway API task configures ingress with Kubernetes Gateway and HTTPRoute resources whose acceptance is reported in resource status

GeneratingPolicy data-source table (Sync / NoSync): delete downstream recreated / deleted; delete policy deleted unless orphaning is enabled / retained; delete trigger deleted / no effect; modify downstream reverted / modified; modify policy synced / unmodified; modify trigger deleted / no effect
sources.section: Synchronization with a Data Source (behavior table)

sources.claim: GeneratingPolicy clone-source table (Sync / NoSync): delete downstream recreated / deleted; delete policy retained / retained; delete source deleted / retained; delete trigger deleted / no effect; modify downstream reverted / modified; modify policy unmodified / unmodified; modify source synced / unmodified; modify trigger deleted / no effect
sources.section: Synchronization with a Clone Source (behavior table)

sources.claim: ImageValidatingPolicy v1 has failurePolicy (Ignore or Fail) and webhookConfiguration.timeoutSeconds (default 10 seconds, range 1 to 30, after which the request fails or ignores the result per the failure policy); unlike ValidatingPolicy, its CRD states no failurePolicy default

At v1.20.0 ValidatingPolicy spec.autogen.podControllers.enabled defaults to true and controllers defaults to all supported pod controllers, while spec.autogen.validatingAdmissionPolicy.enabled defaults to false

Autogen resolves controller names through a built-in table keyed by lowercase plural resource names (daemonsets, deployments, replicasets, statefulsets, jobs, cronjobs); other bare names resolve only through a cluster RESTMapper, which an offline CLI run does not have

The CRD field description for autogen controllers gives Kind names (DaemonSet, Deployment, Job, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, ReplicationController, CronJob), which conflicts with the plural resource-name keys the resolver uses (KYV-E38)

The admission-policy generator creates a native ValidatingAdmissionPolicy only when the policy's autogen.validatingAdmissionPolicy is enabled, skips generation when pod-controller autogen produces configs, and blocks it for exceptions with compensating validations

The v1.20.0 Helm chart defaults resourceFilters to skip Event, Node, ReplicaSet, APIService, TokenReview and SubjectAccessReview kinds and every object in kube-system, kube-public and kube-node-lease; webhooks.namespaceSelector excludes kube-system, excludeKyvernoNamespace is true and webhook matchConditions are empty
The v1.20.0 Helm chart leaves admissionController.replicas unset and admissionController.podDisruptionBudget.enabled false (minAvailable 1); reportsServer.enabled and openreports.enabled are false
A default Kyverno installation provides four separate Deployments, each with a single replica, and high availability is achieved per controller
MutatingPolicy v1 mutations use patchType ApplyConfiguration or JSONPatch; reinvocationPolicy is Never or IfNeeded; targetMatchConstraints and targetMatchConditions select mutate-existing targets
DeletingPolicy v1 has schedule, conditions, matchConstraints, variables and deletionPropagationPolicy (Foreground, Background or Orphan)

kyverno CLI test results declare the policy type with isValidatingPolicy, isMutatingPolicy, isImageValidatingPolicy, isGeneratingPolicy, isDeletingPolicy or isValidatingAdmissionPolicy, and compare patchedResources, generatedResource(s) or cloneSourceResource for mutation and generation

At v1.20.0 PolicyReport and ClusterPolicyReport are served and stored as wgpolicyk8s.io/v1alpha2; results carry policy, rule, result (pass, fail, warn, error or skip), source, timestamp, scored, severity, category, properties and resources, with a summary count per result value

ValidatingPolicy validations carry expression, message, messageExpression and reason; messageExpression takes precedence over message and falls back to it when it fails or yields an empty, whitespace-only or multi-line string; auditAnnotations attach key-value data to PolicyReport results

Kyverno CEL libraries include resource.Get and resource.List, http.Get and http.Post, globalContext.Get, parseServiceAccount, time.now and an image() type whose parts are read with methods such as tag(), digest() and identifier()
sources.section: Resource, HTTP, User, Image, GlobalContext libraries; Time functions

sources.claim: Policy expressions read exception-supplied values through exceptions.allowedValues and exceptions.allowedImages

Published Kyverno example policy verify-image-slsa reads extractPayload(image, attestations.slsaProvenance).builder.id at the top level of the payload; whether in-toto predicate fields sit at the top level or under .predicate is not settled by a source read here
The kyverno CLI Test manifest accepts mock inputs for offline runs: context, variables, userinfo, exceptions, clusterResources, apiCallResponses (url, method, response) and globalContextEntries
